_readme: Hand-authored ground truth for the 10 seed emails, written by reading them.
It is deliberately NOT exact-match. LLM output legitimately varies in wording,
tag vocabulary and how finely it splits entities, so every assertion is a
'must contain' set:
expectedRisk            Exact match scores 1.0, an adjacent band scores 0.5,
anything further scores 0.
minimumAcceptableRisk   Optional floor. Scoring below it counts as a CRITICAL
MISS and is reported separately from the average - a
missed wire fraud is not the same kind of error as a
slightly over-cautious benign email.
requiredTagGroups       Array of synonym groups. At least one tag from each
group must be present. Models name things differently;
the concept is what matters.
forbiddenTags           Tags that must NOT appear. Used on benign emails to
measure precision, not just recall.
requiredEntities        Each must be matched by some extracted entity of the
same type.
requiredRelationships   Each must be matched by some extracted relationship.
Direction matters; type is only checked when typeAnyOf
is given, since our relationship vocabulary is open.
Matching rule for every *AnyOf / match field: the candidate string is
lowercased with '$', ',' and whitespace removed, then tested for substring
containment. So '$184,500' normalises to '184500' and matches '184500'.

cases.label: CEO fraud / business email compromise
cases.notes: Sender domain arclne-corp.com is a typosquat of arcline.com. Urgency, secrecy, out-of-band account details and a large round-ish wire are the classic BEC stack.

cases.label: Routine IT maintenance notice (benign)
cases.notes: Precision control. Internal sender, no ask, no financial or personal data.

cases.label: Insider data exfiltration ahead of resignation
cases.notes: Work address to personal fastmail, stated intent, confidential attachment, explicit instruction to avoid the work email. Attachment text carries the $1.2M / $800K figures.

cases.label: Vendor invoice with redirected bank details
cases.notes: The tell is cross-email: E009 establishes account ending 6621 as the account on file for the same vendor. A single-email model can still flag the unsolicited bank-detail change.

cases.label: Material non-public information tip
cases.notes: Undisclosed deal, trading suggestion, personal address, instruction to delete. Textbook market abuse.

cases.label: Threatening message from external counterparty
cases.notes: Veiled physical threat plus knowledge of the office location. No financial angle - checks that the risk model is not purely money-driven.

cases.label: HR holiday schedule (benign)
cases.notes: Precision control. Has an attachment, so it also checks that attachments alone do not inflate risk.

cases.label: Credential phishing via lookalike domain
cases.notes: Sender domain arclline-portal.com and link host arclline-portal-secure.com are lookalikes of arcline.com. No relationship assertion - this email is about a link, not a party-to-party interaction.

cases.label: Legitimate vendor invoice (benign baseline)
cases.notes: The control for E004: same vendor, normal terms, the account that is genuinely on file. If this scores high, the pipeline is pattern-matching on the word 'invoice' rather than on anomaly.

cases.label: Whistleblower report of accounting irregularity
cases.notes: Deliberately mid-band. The email reports a concern rather than being the misconduct itself, and the reporter is anonymous - a defensible 'medium' rather than 'high'. Adjacent-band scoring means a model answering 'high' still gets partial credit.
